old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a mechanical process involving a yellow anvil placed on a black and yellow striped base. A large, metallic punch press descends from above, positioned directly over the anvil. As the press begins to descend, it exerts pressure onto the anvil, causing it to deform visibly. The anvil's surface starts to crack and split under the force, but no pieces break off or scatter around its base. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing tightly on the interaction between the punch press and the anvil. The background is plain white, ensuring all attention is drawn to the mechanical action taking place. The lighting is bright and even, highlighting the details of the anvil's deformation and the precision of the machinery.

caption: The video captures a compression test where a dark gray tapered blade suspended from a metallic upper platen presses into the center of a yellow-painted, anvil-shaped object. The object rests on a yellow-and-black diagonally striped cylindrical base against a plain light gray wall. The platen and blade translate steadily downward, driving the blade tip deeper into it. The yellow object deforms under the load, its flat top folding downward around the contact point while the right wing tilts upward and the left horn bends and crumples. Cracks open along the fold lines, exposing gray metal beneath, and this bare-metal area widens as the descent continues. The base, striped cylinder, and background remain fixed, indicating no camera motion. The crushing is gradual, already underway in the first frame and still in progress at the last, with no discrete start or stop visible within the excerpt.

infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.
Retain its English narrative voice, viewpoint, paragraph structure and level of visual detail.

and retain supported scene details while clearly describing the main visible process. Do not
replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.
Correct wrong subjects, actions, directions, contacts, temporal ordering and completion claims.
Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.

"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
